question_type: two monthly table cells summed, then converted with an external (non-corpus) exchange rate rounded to 2 dp; column-selection trap among look-alike receipts columns
decisive_step: Pick the 'Federal receipts from the public' column (net of intragovernmental deductions) of the Cash Income and Outgo tables for the January and February 1956 monthly rows, not the neighbouring 'Receipts > Total' (budget + trust before deductions), 'Budget (net)' or Table 2 'cash deposits' columns; the reference made this choice at treasury_bulletin_1956_04.txt:627 (header) and :646-647 (rows), cross-checked by the Table 3 identity at :716-717 (worklog step 2; solution.json decision 1). The two values are identical in every printing 1956_04..1957_02 (worklog step 3), so vintage is immaterial. The USD/INR rate is absent from the corpus (worklog step 4) and must come from external knowledge: the fixed 1949-1966 rupee par, rounded to two decimals as the question instructs.

smallest_change.change: No correctness change needed: all four cells and the reference agree. The one thing every cell had to work around is a tool defect (see alternatives): printings reported the deductions cell of the 1957_02 and 1956_08 printings, and a single-digit cell of 1956_12, under the label 'Equals: Federal receipts from the public', because the header parse of those printings is shifted by one column while the data columns are not.

alternatives.change: In otables.py/printings: when the same (table, row, column-label) is matched at different column indexes across printings (here c7 in 1956_03/1956_08, c8 in 1956_04..1957_01, c9 in 1956_12) or when the matched column's identity check contradicts its label (show_table's note 'identity: c7 = sum c4..c6' proves c7 is the deductions total, not 'Equals: Federal receipts'), print a warning line under the summary: 'WARNING: column index differs across printings (c7/c8/c9) and c7 of 1957_02 satisfies the deductions identity; the label may be shifted one column left. Compare with show_table <file> <line> --grep <row> before trusting the latest value.' Also, when a cell carries [multi:2] (two numbers in one cell, as in 1956_03:709), list both numbers as separate candidates instead of one string.
alternatives.why_not_first: All cells recovered by opening the raw lines, so it changed cost, not correctness; but the 'latest printing' summary line stated a wrong-column value as the latest revision, which the later_printing rule (b2) would happily have offered as a substitute on a question where the model did not look. It is the most concrete tool bug in this question and is domain-general (header/data misalignment).

notes: Three things for v10. (1) Header/data misalignment in printings is real and reproducible on treasury_bulletin_1957_02.txt:1166 (Table 3) and 1956_08.txt:1149: the labels are shifted one column left of the data, and the tool's own identity notes already prove it (c[16]: 'identity: c7 = sum c4..c6' under a column labelled as the receipts total). The mech-static later_printing rule, which substitutes the latest printing, would have offered a wrong-column value here if the model had not looked; printings should carry the warning line described above, and the substitute_printing offer should be suppressed when the column index of the match differs from the majority of printings. (2) printings --col with the question's phrase 'Total receipts from the public' matched nothing (c[8]); a fuzzy 'did you mean: Equals: Federal receipts from the public / Receipts > Total' line would save a step. (3) The external-constant hunt is the dominant cost (15-35 steps per cell, ~70% of c's run); a one-line text rule to search twice then use standard knowledge, or a small lookup note in README for the handful of external constants the benchmark uses (exchange rates, CPI), would cut it without affecting correctness. Cell a answered with units appended ('... million INR') and was still graded correct; the answer-format guidance did not need to fire. The v8 per-question file listed in index.json (003.json) does not exist because v8 analysed only GLM-fail/Opus-pass questions.
